quizzes.title: Brazil, Israel and Finland Ties
quizzes.passage: India's relations with partners across several continents moved forward in early 2026 through state visits, new agreements and participation in global forums. The most prominent visit was the state visit of the President of Brazil, which followed the Prime Minister's trip to Brazil in July 2025. The two countries reaffirmed their long-standing strategic partnership and agreed to deepen cooperation in trade, the digital economy and strategic sectors. Trade was another focus, and both sides set a long-term bilateral trade goal for the end of this decade. A joint declaration on digital partnership was adopted, covering digital infrastructure, artificial intelligence and emerging technologies. Their talks also covered energy transition and climate change, and the Prime Minister commended Brazil for hosting a major climate conference. Defence and space cooperation also featured in the discussions, which covered shared technology and innovation priorities. Relations with Israel were raised to a special strategic partnership level, reflecting closer cooperation in defence, technology and innovation. Separately, India and Finland agreed to elevate ties during a visit linked to the Raisina Dialogue, a forum launched in 2016 that discusses global governance, security and economics. Finally, the Takeshima and Dokdo islets remain a sovereignty dispute between Japan and South Korea, which protested a Japanese government-backed event in Shimane Prefecture.

questions.q: Which satellite, launched by India in 2021, is Brazil's first fully indigenous Earth observation satellite?
questions.explanation: India launched Amazonia-1 in 2021 as Brazil's first fully indigenous Earth observation satellite.

questions.q: In which year did French whalers name the Liancourt Rocks?
questions.explanation: French whalers named the islets Liancourt Rocks in 1849.

questions.q: In which year was the Brazil-India Strategic Partnership established?
questions.explanation: The Brazil-India Strategic Partnership dates to 2006, while diplomatic relations were established in 1948.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Takeshima/Dokdo dispute is rooted in Japan's colonial rule over Korea.
Reason (R): Japan ruled Korea as a colony from 1910 to 1945.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R explains A
Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet traces the dispute to the legacy of Japan's colonial rule over Korea, which lasted from 1910 to 1945.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Israel   ->   D. Holds 94% of niobium reserves
II. South Korea   ->   A. Up to 50,000 Indian workers over 5 years
III. Finland   ->   C. Aims to double bilateral trade by 2030
IV. Brazil   ->   B. Permanent coastguard detachment on the islets since 1954
questions.explanation: Israel will allow up to 50,000 Indian workers, South Korea has kept a coastguard detachment since 1954, Finland aims to double trade by 2030, and Brazil holds 94% of niobium reserves.

questions.q:
Examine the statements below:
I. Japan claims it formally incorporated the islets in 1905 as terra nullius.
II. The 1951 San Francisco Peace Treaty explicitly named the islets among the territories Japan was to return.
III. Dokdo is South Korea's name for the islets and means Solitary Island.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement II is false because the treaty did not explicitly name the islets, while I and III match the booklet.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
1. The Indo-Finland Startup Corridor will connect India's Startup Mahakumbh with Finland's Slush.
2. Japan's name for the islets, Takeshima, means Bamboo Island.
3. India and Brazil signed a Critical Minerals MoU covering iron ore.
questions.explanation: Statement 3 is false because the Critical Minerals MoU covers rare earths, lithium, graphite, niobium and nickel, while iron ore was in a separate steel MoU.

quizzes.title: Diplomacy and the Islet Dispute
quizzes.passage: India's diplomacy in early 2026 combined high-level visits with agreements on trade, technology and workforce mobility. The President of Brazil made a state visit to India, and the two countries adopted a joint declaration on digital partnership covering digital infrastructure, artificial intelligence and emerging technologies. The visit was accompanied by several sector agreements. Brazil's President also received an invitation to the BRICS 2026 Summit in India. Their strategic partnership dates back to 2006, and the two sides also discussed critical minerals, defence and food security. Ties with Israel were upgraded to a special strategic partnership, with new cooperation in cybersecurity, semiconductors and space technology. The Israel arrangements also addressed labour mobility over the coming years. In Europe, India and Finland agreed to elevate their relationship in digitalisation and sustainability during a visit linked to the Raisina Dialogue, a forum launched in 2016. Japan and South Korea continue to dispute a pair of islets that Japan calls Takeshima and South Korea calls Dokdo. The dispute is rooted in Japan's colonial rule over Korea, and the islets were not explicitly named in a 1951 peace treaty. Both countries describe the islets with names that reflect their sovereignty claims, which makes the matter politically sensitive. South Korea has protested a Japanese government-backed event held in Shimane Prefecture.

questions.q: Who was the Chief Guest at the 11th Raisina Dialogue held in New Delhi in 2026?
questions.explanation: Finland's President Alexander Stubb was the Chief Guest at the 11th Raisina Dialogue 2026.

questions.q: In 2025, bilateral trade between India and Brazil reached how many US$ billion?
questions.explanation: Bilateral trade between India and Brazil had already reached US$15.21 billion in 2025.

questions.q: What percentage of global niobium reserves does Brazil hold?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that Brazil holds 94% of niobium reserves.

questions.q: The validity of multiple-entry tourist and business visas was extended from 5 years to how many years?
questions.explanation: The validity of these visas was extended from 5 years to 10 years.

questions.q: Which Indian firm will set up an E175 jet assembly line with Embraer?
questions.explanation: Embraer will set up the E175 jet assembly line with Adani Defence & Aerospace.

questions.q: Israel will allow up to how many Indian workers over the next 5 years?
questions.explanation: Israel will allow up to 50,000 Indian workers over the next 5 years.

questions.q: Which Brazilian city hosted COP30?
questions.explanation: PM Modi commended Brazil for hosting COP30 in Belém.

quizzes.title: Immunisation and Water Programmes
quizzes.passage: Health and water programmes in India have increasingly focused on delivery to citizens. The Universal Immunisation Programme is among the largest public immunisation efforts in the world, and it provides free vaccines to infants, children and pregnant women. Intensified drives have targeted areas where immunisation coverage was low, and a later round focused on children and pregnant women who missed doses during the Covid-19 pandemic. Digital tracking of vaccination records is also supported, and the programme is designed to reach every eligible child. Vaccination drives are planned for children up to two years of age. On water, the Jal Jeevan Mission was extended to the end of 2028 with a shift from building infrastructure to citizen-centric service delivery. Under the extension, the government aims to provide functional household tap connections to all rural households. Water supply systems will also receive unique service area identifiers, which will help track water supply and service delivery. The mission's standards also emphasise community ownership, transparency and accountability. On the environment side, India reports its biodiversity commitments under the Convention on Biological Diversity, and the Nagoya Protocol governs access and benefit-sharing for genetic resources. Reports to the convention are periodic, and each signatory must describe the measures it takes to implement the treaty.

questions.q: Which ministry launched Mission Indradhanush?
options: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
questions.explanation: Mission Indradhanush was launched by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.

questions.q: In which year was the Jal Jeevan Mission launched?
questions.explanation: The Jal Jeevan Mission was launched in 2019 under the Ministry of Jal Shakti.

questions.q: In which year was the Nagoya Protocol adopted?
questions.explanation: The Nagoya Protocol was adopted in 2010 at Nagoya, Japan, and entered into force in 2014.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Jal Jeevan Mission was launched under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.
Reason (R): Jal Jeevan Mission (Urban) is implemented by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R explains A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
questions.explanation: The rural Jal Jeevan Mission was launched under the Ministry of Jal Shakti, while the urban version is implemented by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Mission Indradhanush   ->   D. Tap connections for 19.36 crore rural households
II. Intensified Mission Indradhanush 1.0   ->   B. Water supply standard of 55 litres per capita per day
III. Jal Jeevan Mission   ->   A. Full immunisation of more than 90% targeted by December 2018
IV. Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0   ->   C. Launched on 25 December 2014
questions.explanation: Mission Indradhanush launched on 25 December 2014, IMI 1.0 targeted over 90% full immunisation by December 2018, the Jal Jeevan Mission sets 55 litres per capita per day, and JJM 2.0 targets 19.36 crore households.

questions.q:
Examine the statements below:
I. Mission Indradhanush targets 12 vaccine-preventable diseases.
II. India was certified polio-free in 2014.
III. U-WIN is a digital platform for tracking land records.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: U-WIN is a digital platform to track vaccination records, not land records, so statement III is incorrect.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
1. Gram Panchayats and Village Water Committees take part in the Jal Arpan handover protocol.
2. The Nagoya Protocol entered into force in 2014.
3. The Convention on Biological Diversity was adopted at the 1992 Rio Earth Summit.
questions.explanation: All three statements match the booklet: Jal Arpan involves Gram Panchayats and Village Water Committees, Nagoya entered into force in 2014, and the CBD was adopted at the 1992 Rio Earth Summit.

quizzes.title: Vaccination, Water and Biodiversity
quizzes.passage: India's public health and water programmes have been revised to focus on regular delivery and sustained coverage. The Universal Immunisation Programme was re-launched in 1985 and offers free vaccines to infants and pregnant women against several vaccine-preventable diseases. Intensified drives have targeted districts where coverage is 70% or below, and a later drive reached children who missed doses during the Covid-19 pandemic. Mission Indradhanush aims to give full immunisation to children up to two years of age, and it is supported by a digital platform. Water policy has moved in a similar direction. The Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 extends work to December 2028, with its focus on citizen-centric service delivery rather than infrastructure alone. Under the Jal Arpan initiative, completed water infrastructure is handed over through a formal protocol involving Gram Panchayats. India's biodiversity commitments run alongside this, and the Convention on Biological Diversity requires member countries to submit periodic reports on the measures they take. India has also submitted its first national report under the Nagoya Protocol, which covers access and benefit-sharing mechanisms. The reports highlight progress in conservation, sustainable resource use and fair sharing of benefits from biological resources. Monetary and non-monetary benefits both count under this framework. Such progress is reported at regular intervals.

questions.q: In which year was Intensified Mission Indradhanush 1.0 launched?
questions.explanation: Intensified Mission Indradhanush 1.0 was launched in October 2017 with a target of over 90% full immunisation by December 2018.

questions.q: On which day of March is National Vaccination Day observed?
questions.explanation: National Vaccination Day is observed on 16 March.

questions.q: In which year was India certified polio-free?
questions.explanation: India was certified polio-free in 2014.

questions.q: What are the Village Water Committees also called in the Jal Arpan handover protocol?
questions.explanation: The Village Water Committees are also called Paani Samitis.

questions.q: What is the water supply standard, in litres per capita per day, under the Jal Jeevan Mission?
questions.explanation: The Jal Jeevan Mission uses a water supply standard of 55 litres per capita per day.

questions.q: What digital platform is used to map drinking water infrastructure?
questions.explanation: The Sujalam Bharat Digital Platform is a new platform to map drinking water infrastructure.

questions.q: How many years is the generally followed cycle for India's national reports under the Convention on Biological Diversity?
questions.explanation: National reports under the CBD are generally submitted every 4 years.

quizzes.title: Reserves, Security and Navigation
quizzes.passage: India's economic and security agenda in early 2026 touched on trade rules, reserve management, state finances, counter-terrorism, border infrastructure and satellite navigation. At the World Trade Organization, India opposed bringing an investment-related framework into the main trade system, even though many members supported it. Currency markets also drew attention, as India's foreign exchange reserves fell during the period. The reserves are held by the Reserve Bank of India, which uses them to stabilise the rupee and cushion external shocks. The reserves are governed by the Reserve Bank of India Act and the Foreign Exchange Management Act. Gold, special drawing rights and the reserve tranche position with the IMF are also part of the reserves. The central bank sold dollars at times to manage volatility. On state finances, NITI Aayog released an annual fiscal health evaluation that benchmarks states on quality of expenditure, revenue mobilisation and debt. The index covers major states and north-eastern and Himalayan states, which are ranked separately. In security, the government released a national counter-terrorism policy that promises a zero-tolerance approach. In eastern Ladakh, an airfield drew attention for strengthening India's presence near the border. Satellite navigation also drew attention after a clock failure on one satellite weakened a regional system.

questions.q: Which organisation developed NavIC?
questions.explanation: NavIC is India's indigenous regional navigation system developed by ISRO.

questions.q: In which year was the Mudh-Nyoma Air Force Station built?
questions.explanation: Mudh-Nyoma Air Force Station was built in 1962 in the Changthang region of eastern Ladakh.

questions.q: After which conflict was NavIC initiated?
questions.explanation: NavIC was initiated after the Kargil War of 1999, when India lacked access to foreign GPS for defence use.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): India's forex reserves fell as the US dollar strengthened.
Reason (R): A stronger US dollar reduces the value of euro, yen and pound holdings in reserves.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R explains A
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet attributes part of the reserve decline to the valuation effect of a stronger dollar on euro, yen and pound holdings.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Mudh-Nyoma Air Force Station   ->   A. Relies on audited fiscal data from the CAG
II. NavIC   ->   D. Has seven pillars covering prevention to recovery
III. PRAHAAR   ->   B. Upgraded by the Border Roads Organisation under Project Himank
IV. Fiscal Health Index 2026   ->   C. Requires at least four operational satellites
questions.explanation: Mudh-Nyoma was upgraded by BRO under Project Himank, NavIC needs at least four operational satellites, PRAHAAR has seven pillars, and the Fiscal Health Index relies on CAG audited data.

questions.q:
Examine the statements below:
I. The atomic clock was invented in 1955.
II. NavIC consists of 7 satellites placed in geo-stationary and geo-synchronous orbits.
III. Foreign currency assets are the smallest component of India's forex reserves.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Foreign currency assets are the largest component of forex reserves, not the smallest, so statement III is incorrect.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
1. The IFD Agreement is a plurilateral agreement binding only on its signatories.
2. The Fiscal Health Index 2026 covers FY 2023-24.
3. The Mudh-Nyoma Air Force Station lies close to the northern bank of Pangong Tso.
questions.explanation: Statement 3 is false because Mudh-Nyoma lies close to the southern bank of Pangong Tso, while statements 1 and 2 match the booklet.

quizzes.title: Forex, Fiscal Index and NavIC
quizzes.passage: Several economic and strategic developments in early 2026 reflected pressures in global markets and regional security. India's foreign exchange reserves declined by a notable amount, as the central bank supported the rupee and rising crude oil prices added to demand for dollars. The Reserve Bank of India manages these reserves, which consist of foreign currency assets, gold, special drawing rights and a reserve tranche position with the International Monetary Fund. An international framework on investment facilitation was discussed at the World Trade Organization, and India did not support it. In the same period, NITI Aayog released the Fiscal Health Index, an annual evaluation of states that relies on audited data from the Comptroller and Auditor General. On security, the government's counter-terrorism policy set out a zero-tolerance doctrine. Meanwhile, an airfield in eastern Ladakh drew attention for its high altitude and its proximity to the border. Satellite navigation was also in focus after an atomic clock failure affected a regional navigation system called NavIC, which is developed by ISRO and needs several satellites to work reliably. India's reserve tranche position is a quota-based reserve with the IMF. The reserves are used to stabilise the rupee, finance imports, cushion external shocks and enhance economic credibility.

questions.q: By how many US$ billion did India's forex reserves drop in the reported period?
questions.explanation: Forex reserves dropped by US$7.052 billion to US$709.759 billion.

questions.q: For which financial year does the Fiscal Health Index 2026 evaluate states? Give the answer in the format YYYY-YY.
questions.explanation: The Fiscal Health Index 2026 covers FY 2023-24.

questions.q: The Investment Facilitation for Development Agreement was launched in 2017 at which ministerial conference?
questions.explanation: The IFD Agreement was launched under the Joint Statement Initiative at the Buenos Aires Ministerial Conference in 2017.

questions.q: NavIC stands for Navigation with what? Give the two words that complete the expansion.
questions.explanation: NavIC stands for Navigation with Indian Constellation.

questions.q: How many satellites form the NavIC constellation?
questions.explanation: NavIC consists of 7 satellites placed in geo-stationary and geo-synchronous orbits.

questions.q: In which region of eastern Ladakh is Mudh-Nyoma Air Force Station situated?
questions.explanation: Mudh-Nyoma Air Force Station is situated in the Changthang region of eastern Ladakh.

questions.q: What is the elevation of Mudh-Nyoma Air Force Station, in feet?
questions.explanation: Mudh-Nyoma Air Force Station is at an elevation of 13,700 feet above sea level.
